problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}6{y}^{2}\,dV
$$

where $R$ is the type I region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le x,\,0\le z\le x+y}.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type I Regions

feedback.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}16x\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,0\le z\le x-y},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xy$-plane enclosed between the coordinate axes and the line $y=2x-3$ in the fourth quadrant.
feedback.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}16x\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x-y}16x\,dz]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x-y}16x\,dz]dA & ={∬}_{D}[16xz]_{z=0}^{z=x-y}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}16x(x-y)\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/bddbd1c97fe8cd74f9903dec340495f04401323b8e1236680c57c13b18069eb4.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}16x(x-y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}{\int }_{2x-3}^{0}16x(x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}16x[{\int }_{2x-3}^{0}(x-y)\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}16x{[xy-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=2x-3}^{y=0}dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}16x(0-x(2x-3)+\frac{1}{2}(2x-3)^{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}8x(-4{x}^{2}+6x+4{x}^{2}-12x+9)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}8x(-6x+9)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}-48{x}^{2}+72x\,dx \\  & ={[-16{x}^{3}+36{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=3/2} \\  & =-16{(\frac{3}{2})}^{3}+36{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =-54+81 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$
